name: antiphony
description: Antiphony — standalone call-and-response audio infrastructure (open core extracted from Vox Pop).

scripts.build: npm run build -w @antiphony/shared && npm run build -w @antiphony/core-api
scripts.test: npm run test --workspaces --if-present && npm run test:eslint-rules && npm run test:lexicons
scripts.//test:eslint-rules: The custom ESLint rules in eslint-rules/ carry RuleTester suites that use node:test, not vitest, so `--workspaces` never reached them — they sat unrun since they were written. The glob is quoted because bare `node --test eslint-rules/` also picks up the rule sources themselves and exits non-zero.
scripts.//test:lexicons: Validates lexicons/ against upstream's own encoding of the Lexicon spec (@atproto/lex-document), so a spec change upstream lands as a CI failure rather than a federation-time surprise. Lives at the root, not in a workspace, because lexicons/ is repo-level and belongs to no package. Refs into app.bsky.*/com.atproto.* are reported but NOT resolved — resolving them means vendoring ~20 third-party documents and putting a network fetch or CID-pinned manifest in the CI path (see specs/xrpc-and-atproto-lex-strategy.md §7). The Zod-vs-lexicon parity oracle is separate, in @antiphony/shared's vitest suite.

//allowScripts: npm 12 does not run a dependency's install script unless it is listed here; npm 10 and 11 ignore this field and run them all. Three of these are load-bearing and one fails SILENTLY without its script: ffmpeg-static downloads the ffmpeg binary, and without it ffmpegAvailable() returns false, so the trim and waveform stages advertise themselves as unavailable and posts settle those stages as `skipped` rather than erroring. esbuild fetches its platform binary (core-api cannot bundle without it) and sharp backs Astro's image service in the docs build. @firebase/util, protobufjs, and fsevents (macOS-only) are here because they already run today under npm 10 — this file records the trust that exists rather than making a new decision. Entries are unpinned by name on purpose: `npm install-scripts approve --allow-scripts-pin` writes `pkg@version` instead, which re-blocks on every version bump — and a re-blocked ffmpeg-static is exactly the silent failure above. Add entries with `npm install-scripts approve <pkg>` on npm 12+.
//packageManager: Declares the npm this repo is verified against, for build environments that resolve it (corepack-aware ones do; actions/setup-node does not switch npm on it). The Dockerfile does not rely on resolution at all — it installs this exact npm explicitly, which is the point: production used to build on the Firebase App Hosting buildpack's own npm, and an unreviewed bump to it broke prod. It is safe to land only because `allowScripts` above landed with it: pinning to npm 12 without that list would block the install scripts this repo depends on. Full suite, core-api bundle, and docs build all verified green on 12.0.2.
